tasks.short: Train faculty and media staff in software and equipment

steps.what: Establish learner needs and check installed software and equipment versions
Prepare the demonstration outline and practice instructions
Check demonstration steps against the installed equipment
Train faculty and media staff and supervise hands-on practice

tasks.design: Reuse the existing {DOCS} demonstration-outline headings and practice-step layout. The librarian checks the actual version and equipment, writes current instructions and retains all teaching and hands-on supervision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training must match installed versions and learner confidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native outline reuse removes a small amount of repeated formatting.
tasks.still_hard: Helping people recover when a live demonstration behaves differently.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion and adapt the pace and explanation.
tasks.altitude: Small preparation relief with the same teaching duties.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document outline reuse can shorten formatting, while equipment training still needs version checks and supervised practice.

assumptions: Boundary is an existing prepared training session, not a new course-management process. Shares are provisional.

Learners supply needs in s1; the librarian verifies installed version and reads original equipment instructions before writing s2. No structured transcript or automatically extracted manual is assumed.
Test native {DOCS} layout first. Only fixed heading and practice-list formatting, 6% of s2, is removed; substantive instructions, checks and ordinary saving remain.
No training completion record or handout send is established by this task. If either actually exists, count its first write and any separate gated release; do not invent a trailing training log.
research_questions: Does reusable outline formatting remove time beyond what the current editor already supplies?

already_counted.description: Instruction writing, demonstration checking and live training remain.

incremental.description: Librarian updates the outline when equipment families change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 15*0.06=0.9 formatting hours removed less 0.25 upkeep gives 0.65 net. Cautious case: new equipment requires custom practice sections, leaving 0.30 hours of reusable headings and 0.05 net; teaching remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Locate equipment and verify asset tags, condition and current location
Enter equipment location and condition updates in the asset register
Recalculate equipment counts by location and availability
Reconcile missing equipment and check inventory totals

tasks.design: Test native tagged-asset lookup and location/availability counts in the equipment-asset register category {OTHER}. The librarian still physically verifies equipment and enters actual condition and location; native record lookup removes repeated identity entry and counts replace manual tallying.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical location can diverge from the register, and totals may be rebuilt manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset forms and grouped counts can reuse verified records.
tasks.still_hard: Finding missing units and distinguishing working equipment from merely present equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Verify condition and resolve custody discrepancies.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated identification and tallying, with the same inventory accountability.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset-register lookups and grouped counts can reduce identity re-entry and manual inventory tallying, without replacing physical verification.

assumptions: Boundary includes the existing register used to locate and lend equipment, not a new unused audit log. Shares are unmeasured hypotheses.

The existing register supplies asset identifier, model and registered location; the librarian produces actual tag, location, condition and availability in s1 and captures changes in s2. Missing tags or wrong matches require manual identification within retained s2 and reconciliation s4.

Test native tag lookup and grouped counts before code. s2 loses only repeated asset identity entry, 20%; actual observed fields and ordinary ungated save remain. s3 is today's manual tally effort, not existing automatic runtime; verify it exists before claiming its saving.
No disposal, procurement or custody-transfer approval is automated. Ordinary author updates are ungated; any real commercial or formal transfer action requires its own steps.
research_questions: Can native counts reproduce the current inventory tally without new capture work?

already_counted.description: Physical verification, entry repairs and discrepancy reconciliation remain.

incremental.description: Librarian checks asset lookups and count filters after register changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25*0.20+20=25 hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 24 net. Cautious case: untagged legacy equipment stays manually entered and only one known-location tally saves 4 hours, giving 3 net; physical searching and reconciliation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Reproduce the audio-visual fault and identify the affected setup
Find the matching equipment guide and approved troubleshooting procedure
Test connections and settings and verify restored audio-visual operation
Record tested actions and remaining faults in the existing support ticket

tasks.design: Configure model-specific bookmarks to approved equipment guides in {DOCS}. Keep reproduction, diagnosis, hands-on tests and the actual {HELPDESK} outcome entry; guide retrieval removes navigation rather than deciding a repair.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the correct guide among similar equipment versions can take repeated browsing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document bookmarks expose the original approved guide by model.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, incompatible connections and knowing when specialist repair is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the actual setup and verify the result safely.
tasks.altitude: Less guide navigation; unchanged troubleshooting limits.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: model-specific guide bookmarks can reduce retrieval time while diagnosis and physical checks remain manual.

assumptions: This boundary models equipment faults already arriving as support tickets; the final outcome is read by subsequent support staff. Confirm this actual record rather than adding a new log. Shares are provisional.

The requester supplies the existing ticket; the librarian identifies model/version and reproduces symptoms in s1. Equipment staff maintain original guides; s2 checks model applicability manually. No new structured fault capture or generated diagnosis is assumed.

Test native {DOCS} bookmarks first. Only repeated guide navigation, 20% of s2, is removed; reading, version checking and failed-link fallback remain. The native ticket form does not remove actual observed outcome writing, which stays at 100% with its ordinary ungated save in s4.
No parts order, external escalation send or ticket auto-closure is proposed. Add actual separate releases and their approvals if this workflow includes them.
unknowns: Whether escalation is needed in typical cases
research_questions: Can model-specific bookmarks remove browsing while preserving manual applicability checks?

already_counted.description: Guide checking and fallback remain in s2; fault outcome entry remains in s4.

incremental.description: Librarian checks guide links after equipment or document changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 15*0.20=3 navigation hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5 net. Cautious case: an unfamiliar adapter requires manual guide research, leaving only 0.7 hours of known-model navigation removed and 0.2 net; all diagnosis and record entry stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native equipment records and guide links reduce tallying and navigation; training and troubleshooting remain hands-on.
role.ambitious_version: No automatic repair or expanded technical authority is justified.
